entries.reason: Apple's own header declares -VTFrameProcessorFrame init NS_UNAVAILABLE, so it is not API a caller writes: a frame has no public initialiser, because the processor builds it and an application only hands it to a session.
entries.effect: not carried, and the port implements no -init on VTFrameProcessorFrame, so the class inherits NSObject's and a program that sends it anyway gets a frame with nothing in it rather than a diagnostic - which is precisely what the annotation exists to warn about. Measured on this host's own VideoToolbox (an M4 Pro, tests/backports/host/videotoolbox-frameprocessor): +new responds and answers, -init answers the same object, and a configuration answers frameWidth 0. The failure is silent, which is why the header refuses to compile the send
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTFrameProcessorFrame.h, the NS_UNAVAILABLE on -init; the host's own answer measured through objc_msgSend on 2026-10-03 (a bracketed call will not compile against the annotation)

entries.reason: no session was ever started, so there is nothing to flush or invalidate; -startSessionWithConfiguration:error: returns NO on every call, which is why this is a no-op by construction and not by omission
entries.effect: nothing happens, and calling it on a processor that never started a session is the documented safe order

entries.reason: SDK 26.2's VTFrameProcessor.h:51 declares it and does not mark it NS_UNAVAILABLE, so it is the one way to make a frame processor and the port carries it; it is the one of the family's initialisers that is not NS_UNAVAILABLE, and the other fifteen classes are recorded absent for that reason
entries.effect: a frame processor with nothing started on it, which is what -startSessionWithConfiguration:error: then refuses to start

entries.reason: there is no Metal command buffer to insert anything into on this release, and NO error channel is invented for it: the header returns void, takes no NSError, and SDK 26.2 says only that it performs effects in a Metal command buffer. The gap is Apple's and it is written up in coordination/crutches.md, and every armv7 device answers +isSupported NO before a caller can reach it
entries.effect: nothing is added to the command buffer and nothing is reported; the port cannot report through a channel the header does not have

entries.reason: the same refusal as -processWithParameters:error:, reported through the block. SDK 26.2 says of this method that the completion handler is CALLED when frame processing is completed, so the port RUNS it once with the error rather than leaving a caller waiting; that is a call the header's own words require, not a convenience
entries.effect: the completion runs once, synchronously, with the parameters object that was given and the same NSError -processWithParameters:error: reports

entries.reason: a session never starts on this release, so no processor is ever started, and VTFrameProcessorSessionNotStarted is the code SDK 26.2 defines for exactly that case: the session is used to process frames without being started. A nil parameter is answered first, with the invalid-parameter code, because that answer does not depend on the hardware
entries.effect: NO, with VTFrameProcessorSessionNotStarted (-19732) or VTFrameProcessorInvalidParameterError (-19741) for nil parameters

entries.reason: the same refusal, reported per output. SDK 26.2 says the handler is called once for each destination frame IF NO ERRORS ARE ENCOUNTERED and that the NSError parameter carries an error code; there are no destination frames here, so the one call the handler sees is the one carrying the error, and it is marked as the final output of the request because nothing follows it
entries.effect: the handler runs once with the parameters, kCMTimeInvalid, YES and the same NSError -processWithParameters:error: reports

entries.reason: a release with no VideoToolbox frame processor at all: objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 6.1.3 dyld cache finds no VTFrameProcessor class and no VTFrameProcessor* symbol, so there is no pipeline to build. A nil configuration is answered first and with the invalid-parameter code, because that answer does not depend on the hardware
entries.effect: NO, with VTFrameProcessorInitializationFailed (-19736) in VTFrameProcessorErrorDomain - the code SDK 26.2 gives a pipeline that fails to initialize - or VTFrameProcessorInvalidParameterError (-19741) for a nil configuration

entries.reason: an error domain the header declares as a name and never spells: SDK 26.2 writes `extern NSErrorDomain _Nonnull const VTFrameProcessorErrorDomain` with no string anywhere, so writing it from the name would be a guess. The string is APPLE'S OWN and MEASURED by dlsym on the host's VideoToolbox, which exports the symbol
entries.effect: the port DEFINES VTFrameProcessorErrorDomain under Apple's own measured string, builds every VTFrameProcessor error in it, and tests/backports/host/videotoolbox-frameprocessor compares the bytes against the host's own copy on every run
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTFrameProcessorErrors.h:17 for the declaration; the string measured from /System/Library/Frameworks/VideoToolbox.framework by dlsym on 2026-10-03, which reads "VTFrameProcessorErrorDomain"

entries.reason: Apple's own header declares -VTTemporalNoiseFilterParameters init NS_UNAVAILABLE, so it is not API a caller writes: a parameters object has no public initialiser, because the processor builds it and an application only hands it to a session.
entries.effect: not carried, and the port implements no -init on VTTemporalNoiseFilterParameters, so the class inherits NSObject's and a program that sends it anyway gets a parameters object with nothing in it rather than a diagnostic - which is precisely what the annotation exists to warn about. Measured on this host's own VideoToolbox (an M4 Pro, tests/backports/host/videotoolbox-frameprocessor): +new responds and answers, -init answers the same object, and a configuration answers frameWidth 0. The failure is silent, which is why the header refuses to compile the send
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTFrameProcessor_TemporalNoiseFilter.h, the NS_UNAVAILABLE on -init; the host's own answer measured through objc_msgSend on 2026-10-03 (a bracketed call will not compile against the annotation)
